title: Every pinning on a plane side has access; what the premise still needs
claim: Every pinning on a plane side has access; the premise is reduced to residual classes. (1) The access lemma of ticket A holds with any point p in place of the hub. Re-centred at p, the potentials stay L-natural convex (the section at p of the L-convex set of all solutions of the difference constraints), and the parity reading and the staircase are unchanged, so A's midpoint argument applies verbatim. On a plane knot space with Kasteleyn signs, take untied points p, a (ports and the hub allowed) whose values leave one pattern t on a six-pattern gluing line. If p is, or is tied to, a port, that port is not t's odd port; otherwise p and t's non-odd ports form a near knot excluding a pattern one step from t. (2) PLANAR-COMPOSE A's route lemma holds for any pinning pair. So on a plane near side at a six-pattern removal, every crossing knot pinned by two near points and separated by one far point is generated, for any far side, hub or not. Checked: all 167,704 ordered pinnings on 30 plane spaces have access. On the Fano plane and census 58, none of the 1,536 pinnings by two non-port points does. On splices (six census and two 10-point near sides, four far sides), the 3,438 such knots on plane near sides that no single port separates follow these routes (2,322) or are tie-equivalent to one-sided knots (1,116). (3) Computed, not proved: all 58,875 crossing knots on these splices are generated by one-sided knots together with near-pinned three-point knots, and all 564 new knots are near-pinned three-point knots through the hub on non-planar near sides. The 12,102 residual knots (pinned on the far side, by three near points, or by neither side alone) have no proof. (4) Computed: on plane spaces split at a point, every pinning by two non-port points has access (552); on the Fano plane and census 58 split at a point, no two such points pin.
failure_conditions: A pinning pair on a plane space of neither type (i) nor type (ii) relative to one of its points.
A near-pinned three-point crossing knot on a plane near side, separated by no single port, whose access route fails.
A crossing knot on a tested splice not generated by one-sided knots together with near-pinned three-point knots.
A new knot on a tested splice that is not a near-pinned three-point knot through the hub.
foundation_claim_scope: Plane knot spaces with Kasteleyn signs, one line removed, a gluing line with six port patterns; splices of census and 10-point plane spaces.

validation.independence: Written by Claude in one session at the repository owner's request on 2026-11-02.
validation.status: the access lemma for every pinning pair proved; the remaining premise classified and checked on splices, not proved; no human or external review
validation.novelty: New here; the homogenization of L-natural convex sets is classical (Murota).
